whatItFakes: Conversations omit introducing or asking after relatives shared by the speaker and listener instead of naming their shared relation naturally.
why: The English banks have no shared-parent kin address yet; first names and possessive parent phrases give the wrong relation in these conversations.
replacement: Resolved: a relative two people share is asked after as they call them, by the kin address in src/director/data/journal-rows.json (Dad, Mom, Grandma, Grandpa) or a shared sibling's first name, through the conversation bank's family lines (pool item words-family-talk-kin-address).

whatItFakes: Some spots offer fewer than four replies of four different meaning groups and play with what they have, never padded with a second wording of an answer already offered. The gaps are listed by scene purpose and by everyday subject in src/director/data/reply-gaps.json, and `npm run words:rules` writes each flagged spot under `gaps` in data/english/pulled.json with the groups it offers, how many more it needs and the groups it is missing (no line is queued or pulled for it).
why: The arcs list three moves at many nodes and the banks hold no piece for the fourth move of a group at those scenes and in those everyday subjects, so the composers can only offer what the bank can word; the new replies are the Story session's to write.
replacement: Bank pieces (and arc moves) for each listed gap, written to the scene standard; the entry leaves the gap list when its spot offers four groups.
